args: In selinux/libsepol/cil/src/cil_reset_ast.c, should cil_reset_classpermission() destroy the named classpermission's cp->classperms list shallowly instead of resetting its entries? Please analyze whether this reset function can receive anonymous classpermissions that own their classperms, and compare ownership semantics in selinux/libsepol/cil/src/cil_build_ast.c and aggregation in selinux/libsepol/cil/src/cil_resolve_ast.c.

The reported UAF occurs because cil_resolve_classpermissionset() shallow-appends each classpermissionset statement's owned cil_classperms pointers into a surviving named classpermission aggregation. During optional disable and AST re-resolution, cil_reset_classpermission currently calls cil_reset_classperms_list(cp->classperms), retaining list nodes and borrowed pointers; then disabled optional children and their classpermissionset objects are destroyed. Pre-verification dereferences the dangling aggregation. I am considering changing only cil_reset_classpermission to cil_list_destroy(&cp->classperms, CIL_FALSE), matching named classpermission destruction semantics, while leaving classpermissionset reset unchanged because it owns and must retain its source structures for re-resolution.
